fidelity: F2a — Lumped Adsorption Column with Langmuir Isotherm + LDF Kinetics
source: Ruthven (1984) Principles of Adsorption and Adsorption Processes, Wiley; Yang (1987) Gas Separation by Adsorption Processes, Butterworths; Sircar & Golden (2000) Sep. Sci. Technol. 35(5), 667-687; Glueckauf (1955) Trans. Faraday Soc. 51, 1540 (LDF)

unit.name: Single-bed industrial H2 PSA (activated carbon + zeolite 5A), reformate feed

bed_length_m.note: Adsorption column length. Yang (1987) industrial H2 PSA

bulk_density_kg_m3.note: Adsorbent bulk (bed) density. Activated carbon ~480, zeolite 5A ~750; blended

q_sat_mol_kg.note: Langmuir saturation loading of impurity (CO/CH4/CO2/N2 lumped) on adsorbent. Yang (1987) Table 3.x

b_langmuir_ref_per_bar.note: Langmuir affinity constant b at T_ref for the lumped impurity. Sircar & Golden (2000)

isosteric_heat_J_mol.note: Isosteric heat of adsorption of impurity; sets b(T)=b_ref*exp(Q/R(1/T-1/Tref)). Ruthven (1984)

k_ldf_1_s.note: Linear Driving Force lumped mass-transfer coefficient (macropore-diffusion controlled, H2 PSA). Glueckauf (1955); Ruthven (1984) ch.6; typical 1-15 1/s

feed_h2_fraction.note: H2 fraction in SMR reformate; balance is adsorbable impurity. Sircar & Golden (2000)

T_operating_K.note: Near-ambient isothermal PSA operation. Sircar & Golden (2000)

u_feed_m_s.note: Interstitial feed gas velocity during adsorption step

purge_to_feed_ratio.note: Fraction of product H2 used to purge/regenerate the bed. Sircar & Golden (2000): 0.1-0.25
